messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service=hosted-inference-prod severity=high (incident #12345)
pd-bot: PagerDuty -> Primary on-call (jake) notified. Escalation timer started (2m).
jake: seeing it, jumping in. any immediate customer impact reported? :phone:
maria: metrics show a spike in 5xxs from the inference fleet ~ 30s ago, ~18% error rate for short-text endpoints. dashboards -> https://redwood.prod/hosted-inference-prod/errors
alex: thanks. is this the kv-cache invalidation bug we saw in canary yesterday?
jake: unknown, starting runbook checks. pulling autoscaler and host health.

maria: quick check: GPUs are healthy, host CPU normal, but nginx upstream logs show a flood of 502/504 from the model pods. suspect model runtime OOM or stuck requests.
sre-ops: I'm on infra side. scaling policy didn't kick because controller saw pods Ready (but not accepting). investigating kube liveness.

jake: PD auto-escalation will notify secondary if still unacked. I'm going to ack and coordinate, but if I need a bridge i'll ask. acking now.

pd-bot: PagerDuty -> ACK received from jake at 4135678924
jake: ack. grabbing logs from a failing pod.

maria: paste logs?
jake: copying snippet:
```
2026-03-15T21:15:12Z ERROR inference-serving: worker stuck processing request; queue length=512
2026-03-15T21:15:12Z WARN kvcache: miss spike, mem pressure
2026-03-15T21:15:13Z ERROR runtime: panic: out of memory
```

alex: oof, OOM. looks like a quantization regression from yesterday's model push. can we rollback model:prod:2026-03-15-quant?
maria: I can trigger a canary rollback to v2026-03-14 which was stable.

sre-ops: before rollback, we should divert traffic to fallback variant to avoid capacity churn. running patch to routing policy now.

jake: commands for traffic shift:
```
# route 100% short-text to fallback-model-102
redwoodctl route set --service hosted-inference-prod --route /v1/generate/short --model fallback-model-102
kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-gateway -n inference
```

maria: routing change applied. verifying.

sre-ops: gateway pods restarted, new requests going to fallback. error rate dropping to 2% in last 30s.

jake: great. i'll proceed with model rollback once traffic is stable.

pd-bot: Escalation: primary unacknowledged? (false) else if unacked would notify secondary (alex) and manager (megan).

alex: i've been paged by PD (notification) just FYI. pulling artifact and preparing rollback patch.

maria: quick customer impact note for the incident log: affected short-text endpoints; approx 15-20% failed requests between 21:14:30 - 21:16:40 UTC; no data exfiltration; mitigation in progress.

jake: rollback initiated to model:v2026-03-14 at 4135678968

maria: rollback complete, health probes green. returning traffic to primary model gradually (10% steps). monitoring for regressions.

sre-ops: autoscaler now sees lower queue lengths, pods recovered.

pd-bot: Incident #12345 status: acknowledged by jake; escalations canceled.

megan: (manager) good job team. any customer-facing action needed?
jake: we should post a brief status on status.redwood.ai with incident timeframe and root cause suspected (model quantization causing OOM). i'll draft.
maria: draft status message:
"2026-03-15 21:14 UTC - Partial outage for hosted inference short-text endpoints. Root cause: model variant push caused runtime OOMs. Mitigation: traffic diverted to fallback model and rollback completed. Service recovered at 21:16:40 UTC. Customers may have experienced increased 5xx rates for ~2 minutes. Follow-up: deploy guardrails for model push and preflight memory checks."

megan: schedule a follow-up postmortem with SRE + ML infra + model team. assign owner for preflight checks.

alex: will own preflight memory checks. will add mem/alloc tests to model CI.

jake: closing notes: incident duration ~4m; impact limited by quick routing change. no customer data risk.
maria: adding tags and severity=high -> incident report. thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident #12345 -> Resolved (closed at 4135679048)
